title: Deadline budget
hints: Do the arithmetic once, up front: `deadline, ok := ctx.Deadline()`, `total := time.Until(deadline)`, and the sum of the weights (a weight below 1 counts as 1). Then loop over the steps, computing `budget := total * time.Duration(w) / time.Duration(sum)`.

Put one step in a helper so `defer cancel()` runs per step: `stepCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, budget, &StepTimeoutError{Step: s.Name, Budget: budget})`, then `err := s.Run(stepCtx)`. Watch the order: once `cancel` has run, `stepCtx.Err()` is **always** non-nil, so inspect `stepCtx` before canceling.

In the helper: `if err == nil { return nil }`; `if stepCtx.Err() != nil { return context.Cause(stepCtx) }` (your `*StepTimeoutError`, or the parent's cause if the parent ended first); otherwise `return fmt.Errorf("step %q: %w", s.Name, err)`. In the loop, `if ctx.Err() != nil { return context.Cause(ctx) }` before each step. `Error()` is `fmt.Sprintf("step %q timed out after %v", e.Step, e.Budget)`.
